en: So how should we name functions and methods
then?
Well, here we can also differentiate between
functions or methods which do perform some
kind of operation and that really can be any
kind of operation. It can be an operation
where data in an object gets changed. It can
be a calculation which returns a value.
But the other kind of function we can have a
look at is a function which computes a
Boolean specifically. So which returns a
Boolean value.
Now, for the first case that we have any
kind of operation,
the function or method name should really
just describe that operation.
So for example, getUser makes it really
clear that we're getting some user, maybe
from a database.
response.send makes it really clear that
we're probably sending the response on which
we execute this method.
Now, for the Boolean case, we again wanna
answer a true or false question. Just as
with the properties and variables and
constants. So here, as an exception, our
function could not describe the operation
but instead the result.
And this is really only the case for
Booleans where you wanna do that.
So here, your method or your functions could
be named isValid or something like an isPaid
method on a purchase to return true if that
purchase was paid and false if it wasn't.
Now, just as before, more details are always
great unless they are redundant. So for
example, if we have a function which
retrieves a user from a database,
but it does so by identifying the user by
email, we could name the function
getUserByEmail to make it really clear that
it's not fetching a user by ID or by any
arbitrary criteria, but that it's always the
email.
Now for response.send, on the other hand,
this already is pretty clear.
Something like response.sendResponse simply
wouldn't make a lot of sense. It's clear
that we're sending this response.
For booleans, just as before, we can also
add more details if it makes sense. For
example, if we have a function which
validates email addresses specifically, we
could name the function emailIsValid.
Instead of just isValid.
On the other hand, again, for
purchaseIsPaid, this is already pretty
clear. More details could be added in some
use cases and scenarios,
but in most scenarios, it's probably good
like this.
